events.title: Birth of Abraham Lincoln
events.description: Abraham Lincoln, the 16th President of the United States, was born in a one-room log cabin near Hodgenville, Kentucky. He rose from humble frontier origins to become a lawyer and politician.
events.significance: Lincoln led the United States through the Civil War, preserved the Union, issued the Emancipation Proclamation, and championed the abolition of slavery through the Thirteenth Amendment.

events.title: Birth of Charles Darwin
events.description: Charles Darwin, the English naturalist, was born in Shrewsbury, England, on the same day as Abraham Lincoln. He later undertook the voyage of HMS Beagle, which shaped his scientific thinking.
events.significance: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection, published in On the Origin of Species in 1859, fundamentally transformed biology and humanity's understanding of life on Earth.

events.title: Founding of the NAACP
events.description: The National Association for the Advancement of Colored People was founded in New York City on the centennial of Lincoln's birth by a group of activists including W.E.B. Du Bois, Ida B. Wells, and Mary White Ovington.
events.significance: The NAACP became the leading U.S. civil rights organization, pursuing legal challenges such as Brown v. Board of Education and advancing racial equality throughout the 20th century.

events.title: Abdication of the Last Qing Emperor
events.description: Puyi, the six-year-old Xuantong Emperor, formally abdicated the Chinese throne following the Xinhai Revolution, ending the Qing dynasty.
events.significance: The abdication ended over two thousand years of imperial rule in China and ushered in the Republic of China, beginning a turbulent modern era in Chinese history.

events.title: Senate Acquits President Bill Clinton
events.description: The U.S. Senate voted to acquit President Bill Clinton on both articles of impeachment, perjury and obstruction of justice, with neither charge reaching the two-thirds majority required for removal.
events.significance: Clinton became only the second U.S. president to be impeached by the House and remain in office, shaping later debates over impeachment and partisan politics.
